thread:
Wanda: Quick PR q — in the SOC2 section I used 'we maintain SOC2 controls' but legal said that's ambiguous. thinking: change to 'we maintain controls aligned with SOC 2 principles and industry best practices' and include a tiny audit-log retention + redaction snippet. PR: https://github.com/redwood/docs/pull/1234

Omar: +1 on clarifying. can you add a minimal example that shows a TTL and a pseudonymization step? keeps it practical for engineers.

Wanda: yep, added a draft snippet below in the PR comment. dropping it here for visibility. @sara can you do a quick read for compliance tone?

sara: thanks for the ping. quick note — avoid absolute statements like 'we are SOC2 compliant' in docs unless we link to the cert/attestation. prefer 'we maintain controls aligned with SOC 2 and undergo regular third-party assessments.' small wording tweak.

Wanda: good call. i'll switch the line to: 'Redwood maintains controls aligned with SOC 2 principles and undergoes regular third-party assessments. For audit logs, we provide configurable retention and pseudonymization options.'

kevin: looks good. about the example: keep it language-agnostic but add one short SDK snippet for python showing TTL header and one curl for ops. also add a tiny JSON sample of a redacted audit event so readers see before/after.

Wanda: draft snippets i put in the PR comment (copied):
```json
// sample redaction example
{
  "event_id": "evt_01F...",
  "user": {
    "id": "usr_XXXX",    // pseudonymized id
    "email": "redacted@example.com"
  },
  "action": "token.create",
  "timestamp": "2025-11-12T14:23:00Z"
}
```
```bash
# quick curl showing TTL header for retention
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/audit/events \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" \
  -H "X-Audit-Retention-TTL: 90d" \
  -d '{"event_type":"login","details":"..."}'
```
```python
# python SDK example (pseudo)
from redwood import AuditClient
client = AuditClient(api_key="${REDWOOD_KEY}")
client.log_event({"event_type":"token.create"}, retention_ttl="30d", pseudonymize=["user.email"]) 
```

Omar: LGTM, styling nit: remove inline comments inside JSON code block (// ...) — JSON strict parsers might be annoyed. use explicit "pseudonymized": true or show a before/after pair.

Wanda: good point. i'll change the example to a before/after short pair in the PR.

docs-ci-bot: PR check failed — docs linter: code-block-language should be one of (json, bash, python). Found 'json' with comments. See build log: https://ci.redwood.example/1234/logs

Wanda: thanks bot, fixing now.

sara: also add a one-line callout: "For customers requiring audit evidence, contact support@redwood.com for export procedures and attestation copies." keeps it actionable.

Wanda: adding that. kevin, do you want me to call out default retention values? might be useful (e.g., default 90 days for host API, configurable for Dedicated/Private).

kevin: yes, call out defaults but say they can be configured per-tenant. keep it short.

Wanda: updated PR with all tweaks, removed comments from JSON, added before/after redaction example, added the attestation contact line, and noted defaults. ready for final legal check. @sara can you ack or request changes?

sara: ACK from legal for the wording and contact line. pls add a link to the security page for the SOC2 attestation once it's live, but not blocking.

Wanda: great — i'll merge after CI passes. thanks all :tada:
